html:
The Muslim Brotherhood is a Sunni Islamist movement founded in 1928 in Ismailia, Egypt, by a schoolteacher, Hassan al-Banna. It became the model for political Islamist movements across the Muslim world.

Ismailia was the company town of the Suez Canal Company, and Banna's message answered British power and Western ways with a call to return to Islam in every part of life. The Brotherhood ran mosques, schools, clinics and welfare, and grew to hundreds of thousands of members by the 1940s. It also had a secret armed wing.

Banna was assassinated in 1949. Nasser banned the group after an attempt on his life in 1954 and jailed thousands; in prison Sayyid Qutb wrote works that inspired later jihadists. Branches spread to Syria, Jordan, Palestine (Hamas grew from it) and beyond.

After the Arab Spring, the Brotherhood's Mohamed Morsi won Egypt's presidency in 2012. The army removed him in 2013, and the group was banned again.
sum: The Muslim Brotherhood is a Sunni Islamist movement founded in 1928 in Ismailia, Egypt, by a schoolteacher, Hassan al-Banna. It became the model for political Islamist movements across the Muslim world.
